Verified against RobinMatrix.lean (sha256 matches authored e957b6a5...). stencilRowCoeff (L21-26): filterMap keeps the coeff of each entry whose offset satisfies rowIdx + offset = colIdx (integer, no modular wrapping), then returns 0 for the empty match, the single coeff for one match, or the left-fold sum for several - exactly the 'sum of all matching coefficients' additive semantics the NL question states. buildRobinMatrix (L56-63): entry (row,col) = stencilRowCoeff row col (robinRowEntries ...). The NL proof's entrywise invariance under merging repeated offsets (grouping a finite scalar sum by equal offset; associativity/commutativity of + preserve the sum, matching the foldl over Coeff.add) is correct. The worked example (1,2),(1,-2),(-1,3): offset +1 coeff 2+(-2)=0 so entry at j=i+1 vanishes; offset -1 coeff 3 so entry at j=i-1 = 3 when in-grid; list has 3 pairs, merged list 2 (incl. a zero), at most one nonzero matrix entry per row, and left-boundary truncation when j=i-1 < 0 - all mathematically sound, consistent with the Nat column index / finite gridSize. The honest caveat that list length does not determine access/oracle cost and that collided-label loaders are not automatically reversible is appropriate.
